faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.description: Here are some quick answers to help you understand how Atmos powers your productivity.

items.question: What is Atmos?
items.answer: A development environment for Agentic Builders. It includes multi-agent execution (TUI / GUI), isolated Worktree spaces, and built-in Git Changes, PRs, file editing, browser, and mobile emulator — everything you need to develop.

items.question: How does Atmos relate to agents like Claude Code and Codex?
items.answer: Atmos is where you run those agents. It reuses the agents you already have, so you can more easily manage multiple agents, isolate each agent's workspace, and observe how they are running.

items.question: Is Atmos right for me?
items.answer: If you often run multiple agents, need to develop several projects or features in parallel, or don't want to keep switching between Terminal, IDE, and browser, Atmos is worth a try.

items.question: Is it free? Open source? Do I need an API key or extra fees?
items.answer: Open source (MIT) and free, with no subscription required. Atmos runs agents using your existing Claude, Codex, Cursor, and similar subscriptions.

items.question: How do I run agents in Atmos?
items.answer: You can run any agent in the Terminal for a native agent experience, or use the Atmos Chat UI when you need it (via Native Adapt / ACP).

items.question: Which agents does Atmos support?
items.answer: Atmos supports every CLI-based agent that runs in a Terminal. Chat UI supports mainstream agents and all ACP-compatible agents, including Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, Hermes, Grok Build, and more.

items.question: Can I remotely control agents in Atmos?
items.answer: Yes. Connect all of your computers, VPS instances, and similar machines through the Atmos Relay server, then access them from any computer — or from the mobile app.

items.question: What else does Atmos include?
items.answer: Additional capabilities include, but are not limited to: Skills management (enable / disable skills); Automation for scheduled and automated tasks; quota windows and token usage analysis for each agent; a Canvas workspace for managing any components across workspaces on one canvas (Terminal, Files, PRs, Diffs, and more); and Tasks, where a Kanban board can manage all workspaces in Atmos as well as GitHub or Linear tasks.
